primary_source.title: Structure and Complexity of Bag Consistency
primary_source.read_via: public web PDF text, not author summary

anchors.paraphrase: For two finite bags, equality of exact intersection marginals, integer feasibility and saturated flow are equivalent.

anchors.location: Theorem 2, printed p.11; proof Step 1, p.15
anchors.paraphrase: Hypergraph acyclicity characterizes local-to-global bag consistency. The constructive direction glues exact marginals using the running intersection property.
For acyclic hypergraphs, a global consistency witness can be constructed in polynomial time with support bounded by the sum of input supports.

primary_source.reviewer_boundary: These results concern exact finite bag marginals. They do not by themselves identify a key-erased FK summary with such marginals, preserve arbitrary SQL query answers, or cover all PK/FK/NULL constraints. No originality claim for generic integer-flow gluing is justified.

hand_derivation.origin: Counterexample pattern supplied in parent task; arithmetic independently reconstructed, not independently discovered.
hand_derivation.schema: B -> A <- C, one non-null FK from B to A and from C to A; unique fresh PKs; no additional constraints.
hand_derivation.payload: Two A rows with equal payload a; two B rows with equal payload b; two C rows with equal payload c. PK and referenced-key identities are erased from the abstraction.
hand_derivation.instance_plus: B1,B2 reference A1; C1,C2 reference A1.
hand_derivation.instance_minus: B1,B2 reference A1; C1,C2 reference A2.
hand_derivation.conclusion: Both instances are legal. The same summary does not determine the FK join COUNT, even on an undirected tree. This refutes universal query fidelity, not existence of a legal reconstruction.
hand_derivation.execution: Pure hand reasoning; no SQL, parser, solver, exhaustive enumeration, benchmark, or experimental rerun.
